questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How grandparents in Africa look after young children
The history of mental hospitals in Zimbabwe
Why traditional healers are popular in villages
Grandmothers giving talking therapy on park benches
questions.why: They hear how community grandmothers in Zimbabwe provide therapy on 'grandma benches'.

questions.q: Why did Dr Dixon Chibanda start using park benches?
options: Patients preferred to be outside
He couldn't find free space in hospitals
The government told him to
It was cheaper than renting offices
questions.why: Neil says it proved impossible to find free space in hospitals, so he turned benches into therapy spaces.

questions.q: Why did he choose grandmothers to do the therapy?
options: They have free time and lots of life experience
They had all worked as trained nurses before
They came to the hospital and asked him for work
They all lived close to the hospital in Harare
questions.why: Sam says he recruited grandmothers, who have both free time and plenty of life experience.

questions.q: What did many villagers prefer before the project?
options: Medicine from pharmacies
Talking to their doctors
Traditional faith healers
Keeping their problems secret
questions.why: Sam says many villagers were suspicious of talking therapy and relied on traditional faith healers.

questions.q: How did Dr Chibanda feel at the start of the project?
options: Completely confident
Angry with his colleagues
Excited but not worried
Honestly a bit worried
questions.why: Asked if he was apprehensive, he says, “I was, to be quite honest.”

questions.q: Why did his colleagues resist the idea?
options: There was no evidence and it had never been tried
It would be far too expensive for the health service
They secretly wanted to do the job themselves
The grandmothers refused to take part at first
questions.why: He says colleagues thought it wasn't evidence-based and it had never been done anywhere in the world.

questions.q: How many people have the grandma benches helped?
options: Around 14 million
More than 50,000
About 5,000
Fewer than 20
questions.why: Sam says the benches have empowered over 50,000 people to deal with their problems.

questions.q: According to Dr Chibanda, why does the project work?
options: It uses the latest western methods from Europe
It is run by highly trained professional psychiatrists
It is simple, cheap and run by respected locals
It takes place in modern hospitals in the capital
questions.why: He says it works because it's simple, cheap and run by communities, especially grandmothers.
